forest-ground.purpose: The frame. Header, bottom nav, footer, deepest hero surfaces. A ground, never a small fill.

price-orange.purpose: Fills only — 2.2:1 on white. Primary buttons, selected chips, badges. Never a text colour.

deep-price.purpose: The text-safe accent at 4.97:1. Links, inline emphasis, focus rings, eyebrows.

tile-teal.purpose: Ground for category tiles and product thumbnails — separates artwork from interface chrome.

price-tint.purpose: Warm sand behind a price, and nowhere else. The tag on the goods.

ink.purpose: Body and heading text at 12.3:1. A green-black from the frame's family, not neutral black.

muted.purpose: Secondary text at 5.3:1, desaturated to 5% so it reads as quiet rather than as a colour.

page.purpose: The ground everything sits on. Tinted, never white — a white card needs something to be a card against.

surface-muted.purpose: First step between page and card: wells, inactive chips.

surface-strong.purpose: Second step: inset rows, pressed grounds.

field.purpose: Inputs sit on their own near-white ground so a form is findable inside a dense page.

success-ink.purpose: Text-safe success. The lighter sibling is a ground only.

coral-ink.purpose: Text-safe danger. The lighter sibling is a ground only.

info.purpose: Deep blue banner and informational surfaces.

display.purpose: Hero headlines. Fluid, so it never needs a breakpoint to stay in proportion.

stat.purpose: The number on a metric tile. Tabular figures are mandatory.

body.purpose: Running text. 16px is a floor — smaller triggers iOS input zoom.

eyebrow.purpose: Uppercase labels INSIDE components. Never above a page heading.

technical.purpose: IBM Plex Sans for API keys, identifiers, barcodes, timestamps. Never a costume for 'advanced'.

shadows.name: subtle
shadows.value: 0 1px 2px color-mix(in srgb, #2d4a3a 8%, transparent), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, #2d4a3a 8%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Smallest lift; rarely used at rest.

shadows.name: medium
shadows.value: 0 2px 4px color-mix(in srgb, #2d4a3a 8%, transparent), 0 6px 16px -6px color-mix(in srgb, #2d4a3a 16%, transparent)

shadows.name: strong
shadows.value: 0 4px 8px color-mix(in srgb, #2d4a3a 10%, transparent), 0 12px 32px -8px color-mix(in srgb, #2d4a3a 24%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: The thing under the pointer, and overlays. Applied on hover, not at rest.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out. Every movement and entrance. No bounce or elastic curve exists in this system.

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: Entrances. All decorative — strips out under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The alternative action. White ground, hairline edge.

narrative.overview:
A market stall you can trust before you walk to it. The deep green is the awning that frames everything; the white card is clean stock laid out in daylight; the warm sand under a number is the tag on the goods; and the orange is used the way a shopkeeper uses a price tag - on the thing you can act on, and nowhere else.

The frame carries the brand; the controls do not. This is the system's central tension and it is deliberate. The world is a market stall, but the components inside it are refined and restrained - quiet surfaces, precise spacing, understated states. A button does not perform. Personality lives in the green that wraps every screen, in the sand behind a price, in the mesh drawn into the deepest surfaces - never in the chrome of a control. When those two pull against each other, the frame wins and the control gets quieter.

Everything is built for a phone held in one hand, outdoors, on data that drops - for a shopper and for the shopkeeper running their business on the same device. Density is generous rather than tight: this is not a dashboard that happens to be responsive, it is a phone product that happens to have a desktop layout.
keyCharacteristics: A deep forest frame around a bright, faintly-tinted page - never a white page
Flat surfaces at rest; depth is a response to state, never decoration
One vivid accent, rationed to what is actionable
Fluid type that never needs a breakpoint to stay in proportion
Tabular figures wherever numbers stack, so money lines up
Every decorative motion strips out cleanly under prefers-reduced-motion

rules.name: The Rationed Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange marks what you can act on and what something costs. Nothing else. If more than one element in a viewport is orange, one of them is decoration and must be demoted.

rules.name: The Two Oranges Rule
rules.body: #ff9500 fills, #c04a12 reads. Orange text on a light ground is always Deep Price; dark ink on an orange ground is always Accent Ink. Neither substitutes for the other, ever.

rules.name: The Frame Is Not A Fill Rule
rules.body: Forest Ground wraps a screen. The moment it appears as a small badge, pill, or icon chip, the hierarchy has inverted.

rules.name: The Tinted Ground Rule
rules.body: The page is never #ffffff. Card legibility depends on the page being a step darker than the card.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Any figure that stacks is set in tabular figures. Right-alignment alone does not align digits; proportional numerals go ragged and the column reads as sloppy.

rules.name: The Sixteen Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Body text on any input-adjacent surface is never below 16px. iOS zooms the viewport on focus otherwise, and the user loses their place.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight, size and tracking. A second typeface must earn its place by marking genuinely different content.

rules.name: The Phone-First Shell Rule
rules.body: Below 640px is the primary layout for every persona, retailer included. A surface that only works with a sidebar, a wide table, or a hover has been designed for a device the primary user does not have.

rules.name: The No Horizontal Scroll Rule
rules.body: The page body never scrolls sideways at any width down to 320px. Content that genuinely exceeds the viewport scrolls inside its own container.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A content card at rest has a hairline and no shadow. On hover it takes shadow-strong and lifts 4px. If a card that holds text needs a resting shadow to be legible, the tonal layering underneath it is wrong. Illustrated tiles (category tiles, product thumbnails) are the stated exception, not a precedent: artwork is an object on the page and may carry resting depth.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: No black shadows. Depth is cast in brand green at low alpha.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. Emphasis is a ground, a weight, or a size - never a thicker line.

rules.name: The Designed State Rule
rules.body: Every component that can be empty, loading, or in error has that state designed. Skeletons over spinners past one second; 'New seller' instead of zero stars; a live region mounted before its message changes, not alongside it.

dos: Do frame every screen in Forest Ground (#123824) and place content on the tinted Page (#f0f2f0). Never a white page.
Do use Price Orange (#ff9500) as a fill with Accent Ink on top, and Deep Price (#c04a12) whenever the accent must be read.
Do set every stacking number in tabular figures.
Do design the phone layout first for every persona - the retailer is on a phone too.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest and let depth answer a state change.
Do name any new layer in the z-index scale rather than picking a number.
Do give decorative motion a clean exit under prefers-reduced-motion - nothing may depend on an animation having run.
Do theme the surfaces you did not draw: selection, caret, focus rings and scrollbars all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system.
donts: Don't put a coloured border above 1px on anything - no side-tabs, no accent bars, no thick left edges. This is the single most recognisable tell of a generated interface, and it is banned outright.
Don't use gradient text, glow halos, text-shadows behind coloured text, or bounce/elastic easing. All four were removed deliberately; reintroducing any of them is a regression.
Don't treat the shopkeeper as anything other than a customer. The retailer surface is a product someone chooses to use, not a back-office form they are made to fill in.
Don't borrow from Western grocery-delivery apps - promo tile grids, countdown urgency, discount confetti, basket-size pressure. This market's customer is the shop, not the impulse.
Don't reach for crypto/fintech dark mode - dark surfaces with neon accents and a chart-heavy hero. Wrong signal for real money in a physical local market.
Don't build page structure from same-size icon + heading + text card grids, and never nest a card inside a card.
Don't put an eyebrow above a page heading. The Eyebrow role exists for labels inside components; a heading carries its own weight.
Don't use Price Orange as a text colour, or Forest Ground as a small fill.
Don't rely on hover to reveal anything. There is no pointer on the primary device.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons. Icons are drawn SVG at one consistent stroke weight.
